newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Nov inflation seen at around 2.5 pct - Isco.
newsitem.headline: Italy Nov inflation seen at around 2.5 pct - Isco.

text.p: Preliminary consumer price data from sample cities shows Italy's November annual inflation rate will be around 2.5 percent, down from 3.0 percent in October, state economic research body Isco said.
An Isco report on the Italian economy said the average rate of inflation for 1996 was expected to be 3.9 percent, in line with government forecasts,but would fall to 2.6 percent in 1997.
Isco said the economy is expected to grow 0.7 percent this year, against a government target of 0.8 percent, while gross domestic product growth in 1997 is seen rising 1.2 percent.
But Isco said the increase in output in 1997 would not be sufficient to obtain "significant improvements" in the employment situation.
It said a modest increase in the employment level would result in only a small reduction in this year's 12.1 percent unemployment rate to 11.9 percent next year.

Regarding salaries, Isco said it had taken into account that in the renewal of contracts "contractual increases would be set in a way to incorporate a partial recovery of purchasing power, in line with contracts which have already been renewed".

The institute said that it believed pro capita salaries in 1997 would increase 4.1 percent in the economy as a whole and 4.3 percent in the industrial sector, against 4.9 and 5.2 percent respectively in 1996.
It said the cost of labour in the economy as a whole was expected to decrease from 3.6 percent in 1996 to 3.1 percent in 1997.
